solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Support with victory, beginning to display fresh vigour

blocks.note: to second a motion is to support it

explanation.surface: A campaign backed by a win is starting to look lively again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the first two pieces. 'Support' reads as a noun but works as the verb, as in backing a motion at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the renewed energy a runner feels after the first exhaustion passes.

clue.text: Group of actors in Indian dress cold and mocking

blocks.note: the sari, a draped Indian garment, holds the actors
C = cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A theatre company in saris, standing aloof and sneering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold and mocking' reads as one description of a person; 'cold' is only a letter, and the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sarcastic remarks mock their target.

clue.text: Conservative and Scotsman perhaps relish wearing women’s clothes?

blocks.note: Ross is a typical Scottish man's name, so an example of a Scotsman
a salad dressing is a relish

explanation.surface: A Tory and a Scot who enjoy donning women's outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relish' looks like a verb meaning enjoy; it is the noun, a sauce. The question mark flags that the definition only covers men.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: for a man, dressing as the other sex means wearing women's clothes.

clue.text: Seize part of finger

blocks.note: informal: to catch or pin down a culprit
the hard plate at the fingertip

explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' looks like a hidden-word signal, but no word follows it to hide anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Police nail a suspect when they catch him, and a nail sits at the tip of each finger.

clue.text: Browsing but not buying operating system, desiring to save power

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe inside

explanation.surface: A computer user shopping online for an operating system but trying to save electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: The computing surface steers away from real shop windows, and 'save power' reads as energy saving rather than a letter kept inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: looking at goods displayed in shop windows with no plan to buy.

clue.text: One often scolding horse

blocks.note: a person who keeps finding fault

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps telling off a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a rider scolding a horse; in fact the scolder and the horse are two separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are plain senses: a persistent fault-finder, and a worn-out horse.

clue.text: Waves with Catherine close to chair, one on wheels

explanation.surface: Catherine waves from beside a chair, possibly a wheelchair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waves' reads as a verb for greeting; it is the noun, sea rollers. 'one on wheels' tempts toward a wheelchair user.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful description: a skater stands on wheeled boots.

clue.text: So far, stag party ultimately wild debauch

indicators.note: take the final letter of each of the words before it

blocks.note: last letters of sO faR staG partY

explanation.surface: So far, the stag do has been pretty wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' seems to belong to the party; it is part of the definition. Here debauch is a noun, a bout of wild indulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a debauch is a bout of excess, and the wildest kind is this.

clue.text: Terrible new lines without legality

blocks.note: less = without, as in 'less sugar'; it goes round the rest

explanation.surface: Awful new rules written without any legal basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without legality' tempts toward LAWLESSNESS, the opposite of the answer; 'without' belongs to the wordplay, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name the quality of being within the law.

clue.text: Celt hero unexpectedly put in dress again?

indicators.note: the letters turn up in an order you would not expect

explanation.surface: A Celtic hero surprisingly back in costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in dress' hints at cross-dressing after 2 down; the question mark covers dressing anyone, not just in a frock.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain gloss: the RE- prefix means again and to clothe is to put in dress.

clue.text: Predator starting war — like hell!

indicators.note: starting as in jumping with a jolt, jumbling the letters

explanation.surface: Some predator begins a war, and the war is hell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' looks like 'beginning', which would take first letters; here it means jumping in surprise. The dash hides that 'war' and 'like hell' belong together.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the orca hunts seals and even other whales, a top ocean predator.

clue.text: Chop up her rotten spiky plant

indicators.note: the letters are chopped and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener told to cut down her decayed prickly shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' looks like the rearranging word, but it is fodder; 'Chop up' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain description: hawthorn and similar trees bristle with spikes.

clue.text: Spots source of rare wood

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone spots where a rare timber comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' reads as a verb, sees; it is the noun, a skin outbreak.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an outbreak of red spots on the skin.

clue.text: Perhaps zip more rapidly around north-east

explanation.surface: An instruction to zip around the north-east at greater speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zip' looks like a verb meaning speed along; it is the noun, a zipper, and 'Perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a zip is one of many devices that close clothing.

clue.text: Greek islander and African once docked two points

indicators.note: docked as a tail is docked, cut short

blocks.note: a citizen of Rhodesia, now Zimbabwe
E and S, two compass points, are removed

explanation.surface: A Greek and an African who were once penalised two points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' fits the island surface as a ship in port, but here it means cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonym: a native of Rhodes, the Greek island.

clue.text: City to shine hosting a second games at first

blocks.note: to glow is to shine; it holds the rest

explanation.surface: A city hoping to shine by hosting the Games for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: this city hosted the Commonwealth Games in 2014 and again in 2026.
explanation.definitionFit: A bare category: Scotland's largest city.

clue.text: Heartless decision primarily offending you and me

blocks.note: a referee's call is a decision

explanation.surface: An unkind ruling that offends the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' could suggest removing a middle letter; here it is simply the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: unfeeling toward others' suffering.

clue.text: American capital mostly returned as well

indicators.note: most of OSLO, dropping the final O

blocks.note: OSLO, Norway's capital, without its last letter

explanation.surface: An American's capital came back too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American capital' reads as one thing, like Washington; the A and the capital are separate.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both adverbs add one more item, 'too'.

clue.text: Very wide headgear? Who cares!

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a remark about a very wide hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark after 'headgear' makes it look like a riddle about a sombrero; it is just three pieces in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: both exclamations dismiss something as unimportant.

clue.text: Nuisance when man, a scoundrel, upset another man

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down

blocks.note: a cad is a rogue; turned upside down

explanation.surface: One man upsets another by being a rogue, which is a real nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the emotional kind, done to 'another man'; it only flips the scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a problem that causes worry, like pain in the head.

clue.text: US beacon moving beneath the waves

indicators.note: a moving object does not stay put, so the letters shift out of order

explanation.surface: An American marker light drifting under the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US' reads as the country, but here it is just two letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain gloss: SUB- means under, and the ocean is the waves.

clue.text: Canopy starting to lose roof

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof is the top letter, which goes

blocks.note: dawning = starting, beginning; its top letter D is removed

explanation.surface: A canopy that's beginning to lose its roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting to' reads like a first-letter signal; it is a whole word meaning beginning, and 'to lose roof' takes its top letter off.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sheet of canvas stretched over a shop front or window.

clue.text: Facade fashioned of garnet

indicators.note: the letters are fashioned into a new shape

explanation.surface: A building front made from garnet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' reads as 'made of' in the surface but is two letters of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the front face of a building.

clue.text: Completely deplete in a beneficial way

explanation.surface: Advice to run something down completely, for good purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the reverse of the clue's order, which reads naturally as a phrase about consuming everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: doing something to good effect.

clue.text: Cause problem with fresh North Sea prawn being prepared

annotation.answer: THROW A SPANNER IN THE WORKS

blocks.note: something in the works is being prepared

explanation.surface: A cook with fresh North Sea prawns heads for trouble in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'North Sea prawn' is rearranged; 'being prepared' supplies the end of the phrase whole. A spanner is a wrench.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: jamming a tool into machinery stops it, so the phrase means sabotage a plan.

clue.text: Company engages fool in Italian town

blocks.note: CO = company; it wraps the rest

explanation.surface: A firm hires a clown in an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like part of 'in Italian town' but it is part of the contents, not a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bare category: a town in central Italy, known for the WWII battle of Monte Cassino.

clue.text: Nonchalance of carrier releasing large ship

indicators.note: to release something is to let it go

blocks.note: AIRLINE, an air carrier, releasing L
L = large, the letter taken out

explanation.surface: A shipping carrier casually letting a big vessel go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrier' in a ship surface suggests an aircraft carrier; it is an airline, and 'large ship' is two separate things.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: an airy manner is light and unconcerned.

clue.text: Words on delivery vehicle repelled enemy

explanation.surface: A delivery van beating off an attacker, with its slogan painted on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery vehicle' reads as a van; the definition is 'Words on delivery', meaning on a delivered letter, and only 'vehicle' is the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic gloss: the phrase, written c/o, goes on a letter sent via someone else's address.

clue.text: Mentioned option when promoting pawn — continue the celebrations!

indicators.note: the phrase is said, not spelt

blocks.note: a chess pawn reaching the far rank may be promoted to a knight

explanation.surface: A chess player chooses what the pawn becomes, then parties on.
explanation.walkthrough: Promotion usually means a queen, so the knight option is the less obvious one the clue wants.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to keep a celebration going late into the night.

clue.text: Come last? Raise then briefly raise again

blocks.note: to bring up a child is to raise it
to rear is to raise, a second word for it

explanation.surface: A worried bidder at the back is told to raise, then raise once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'again' just says that 'raise' is used a second time, now with a different synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to be at the back of a line or procession.

clue.text: Tyrant doesn’t finish phone charging location?

indicators.note: BULLY loses its last letter

blocks.note: BULLY, a tyrant, minus its final Y

explanation.surface: A bully who leaves a phone half charged, wondering where to plug in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charging location' suggests a spot to charge a phone; it is where a bull charges.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic gloss: the arena where bulls charge in a bullfight.

clue.text: Able to spin nonsense with a Conservative

blocks.note: a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician adept at spinning rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The political surface makes 'spin' mean media spin; here it means turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain gloss: something rotatory turns about an axis.

clue.text: Personal assistant with property that’s leased from mum and dad

blocks.note: a leased property; 'with' just attaches it

explanation.surface: An assistant renting a flat from their parents.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the parents the landlords; in fact 'from mum and dad' is the definition, and the lease is only wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain gloss: coming from one's mother and father.

clue.text: Badly cut northerner to finally start improving

indicators.note: the letters are badly arranged

explanation.surface: An injured man from the North who is at last on the mend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly cut' reads as a wound, but 'Badly' alone is the signal and 'cut' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: passing the worst point of an illness or crisis and beginning to recover.

clue.text: Lack winter clothing mostly to the north of settlement

indicators.note: SCARF without its last letter
in a down clue, the first piece sits above the second

blocks.note: SCARF, a winter garment, minus the F

explanation.surface: A northern town short of warm clothes for winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the north of' only makes sense in a down clue, where it means 'written above'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a shortage of something.

clue.text: Willing to stuff cotton fibre body part

blocks.note: lint is soft cotton fibre; it holds GAME

explanation.surface: A body part ready to be padded with cotton wadding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' opens the clue like a description of someone eager, but it is a synonym placed inside the fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: tissue binding bone to bone, one part of the body.

clue.text: Reflection is illusion, featuring upside-down golden lip

blocks.note: a mirage is an optical illusion; it holds the rest
or is gold in heraldry; turned over
the lip of a cup is its rim

explanation.surface: A reflected face is only an illusion, with a gold-painted lip shown upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'golden' is turned over; 'lip' stays the right way up, though 'upside-down golden lip' reads as one inverted object.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the reversed image you see in a mirror.

clue.text: First aid team’s celebration for yoga practitioners?

blocks.note: a group of bearers carrying the injured
whimsically, a do for people who stretch

explanation.surface: Paramedics throwing a party for the yoga class.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a joke reading: yoga devotees are 'stretchers', and a celebration is a party. The question mark flags the invented sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A real term for a team of stretcher-bearers, reread as a party for people who stretch.

clue.text: Committees criticize the Spanish head of state

explanation.surface: Committees attacking the Spanish head of state, the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of state' looks like a title such as king; it is only one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: small groups appointed to judge or advise.

clue.text: Not rigid about initially inducing animal to beg

blocks.note: supple = flexible; it goes round the rest

explanation.surface: Coaxing a flexible pet to sit up and beg.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures teaching a dog to beg; the animal is a different pet and the begging is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal synonym: to plead humbly, as a supplicant does.

clue.text: Measure area for tourists

blocks.note: a step taken, the sense in 'as a last …'
a holiday town, such as a seaside one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Measure' suggests size; it means a step taken, the sense in 'last resort'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are real senses: an expedient you fall back on, and a holiday destination.

clue.text: Begins attacks

explanation.walkthrough: With only two words, the solver must spot a phrasal verb that fits both; 'attacks' as a noun is the false reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idiomatic senses of one phrasal verb: start on a job, and lay into a person.

clue.text: One who may buy bespoke gear regularly

explanation.surface: A shopper who might order made-to-measure kit on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' reads as 'often'; it takes every other letter. Bespoke is British for made to measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a shopper, someone who buys or may buy from a business.

clue.text: Complaint about giant bird originally coming from Africa

definitions.note: 'from Africa' is broad: this is one way of being from Africa.

blocks.note: a moan is a complaint; it goes round the rest
the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A grumble about a huge bird that came from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a definition by example, fair only because the answer is an African nationality; 'coming' reads as part of it but gives one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a native of Morocco, in north-west Africa.

clue.text: Name on kitchenware the wrong way round continuously

explanation.surface: A name printed backwards on the pans, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like a positional link but is taken literally as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: without stopping or a break.

clue.text: Problem in head ruined cosy ships?

indicators.note: the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A nautical problem up at the headland where snug boats were wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' suggests a headland; it is the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose, informal gloss: a severe mental disorder, a problem inside the head.

clue.text: Dancer’s boss shuns a villainous character in capital city

blocks.note: Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer
Iago, the villain of Shakespeare's Othello

explanation.surface: A ballet company's manager avoiding a nasty piece of work in a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancer’s boss' looks like a ballet director; Dancer is a reindeer, so the boss is Father Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A bare category: the capital of Chile.

clue.text: Nepal got irrationally upset with art and culture institution

indicators.note: the letters are upset, knocked out of order

blocks.note: joined 'with' the rest of the fodder, 3 letters

explanation.surface: Nepal got irrationally angry with an art and culture body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irrationally' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder, and 'art' seems to belong to the definition. The answer is a London museum.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a London gallery of portraits, one of the capital's cultural institutions.

clue.text: Flyer advanced by way of ruses we’re told

indicators.note: the word is heard, not spelt

explanation.surface: A flyer promoted by trickery, so we hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests a leaflet; it is a pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated word for a woman pilot, one who flies.

clue.text: Modest roadside accommodation out of bounds for Native American

indicators.note: MOTEL loses its bounds, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A shy motel off-limits to a Native American guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native American' suggests a person; it is an animal native to America.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic gloss: a wild dog native to North America.

clue.text: Money from some tuxedo shops

indicators.note: the answer is some of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Cash spent in dinner-jacket shops.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is British slang, so a non-British solver may not know it.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: informal British slang for money.

clue.text: Fan favourite not doing anything for the audience

indicators.note: what an audience hears, not what it reads

explanation.surface: A star loved by fans who stands before an audience doing nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audience' fits the pop-star surface but is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a star adored by fans.

clue.text: Part of church recalled in prince’s palace

indicators.note: called back, so read backwards
the letters are found in the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters straddle princE’S PAlace; read them backwards

explanation.surface: A chapel recalled from a prince's palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reads as remembered; it means called back, read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain gloss: the rounded end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Hard ignoring son’s argument

explanation.surface: A hard parent ignores a son's quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'son’s' looks possessive, owning the argument; it is just one letter, and the argument is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a petty quarrel.

clue.text: Play featuring one old model

blocks.note: a drama is a play; it holds the rest

explanation.surface: A play starring a former fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old model' reads as a veteran of the catwalk; 'old' is O and 'model' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain gloss: a three-dimensional scale scene, a kind of model.

clue.text: Satisfy primate eating vegetables

indicators.note: what you eat ends up inside you

blocks.note: an ape is a primate; it holds the rest

explanation.surface: Keeping an ape happy by letting it eat its greens.
explanation.walkthrough: The vegetables go in after the ape's P, not after its A, which is easy to get wrong when writing it in.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to placate someone by meeting their demands.

clue.text: Self-esteem, for example, supported by love

explanation.surface: Confidence, say, propped up by love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for example' seems to modify 'Self-esteem', but it is wordplay; 'supported by' works because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: one's sense of self-worth.

clue.text: Sitcom finishes on last day of work week

explanation.surface: A TV comedy series finishing its run on a Friday.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the reverse of the clue's order: 'finishes on Friday' puts the finishing after the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A bare category: a long-running American sitcom about six friends in New York.

clue.text: Sharp tool is dear, possibly?

blocks.note: a paper knife for slitting envelopes
'Dear' is how a letter often begins

explanation.surface: A knife that someone says may be expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dear' seems to mean costly; it is the first word of a letter, as in 'Dear Sir'.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade for slitting envelopes, and cryptically the word that starts a letter.

clue.text: Develop mascot for a heraldic symbol

indicators.note: the letters develop into a new form

explanation.surface: Designing a team mascot as a heraldic emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a' reads as a link to the definition but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain gloss: the heraldic design borne by a family or institution.
